newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude firms but wet activity subdued.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude firms but wet activity subdued.

text.p: Brent crude outright values firmed as did intermonth paper spreads, particularly further into the winter months, but wet activity was subdued as traders awaited the first November Brent barrels.
December Brent was talked around screen levels of $24.10 a barrel after slipping to a low of $24.70/75 earlier in the day on the IPE.

Paper spreads firmed on the day with December bid three cents up at 48 cents against offers of 52 cents. Dec/Jan was discussed at +65/+69 cents and Jan/Feb at +69/+74 cents. Dec/Jan traded at +66 cents.
Differentials held on the physical market with sellers seeking higher numbers due to the tightness of supply in the first decade, particularly for Brent and Ekofisk.
The first November Brent cargoes are due to pass down the paper chains on Friday, and traders said their fate would provide further direction.
"Basically we are still bullish. Refining margins are reasonable and heating oil stocks are low. Also, the loading programmes are perhaps shorter than people thought," a wet trader said.
A cargo of Gullfaks C loading Nov 8-10 was sold at Dated Brent +66 cents. The reported sale of a Forties cargo loading Nov 10-12 at around Dated +54 cents could not be confirmed.
The holder of a Nov 11-13 Statfjord cargo denied selling it, and said it was going into the company's own system.

In the Med market, traders were waiting for the outcome of price talks with Syria and Algeria. Algeria's Sonatrach is looking to raise Saharan Blend by 10-20 cents a barrel for November, with buyers pressing for a rollover.
